title: You think God is silent…
paragraphs:
But what if He already spoke—
and you just got too comfortable to hear Him?

Because in —that image you just saw—nothing looks sinful at first glance.
There’s no obvious rebellion. No idols carved. No blood on hands.
Soft couches. Full tables. Easy laughter.
And a prophet standing in the middle of it all like a disruption they didn’t ask for.
Here’s the tension most people miss:
They weren’t destroyed for what they did wrong…
They were warned for what they stopped feeling.

The Book of Amos records it with terrifying clarity—“Woe to those who are at ease in Zion… who lie on beds of ivory… who drink wine in bowls… but are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph” (Amos 6:1, 4–6).

You can sing worship songs
while your heart slowly drifts.

You can pray in public
while ignoring God in private.

You can be blessed…
and still be spiritually asleep.
Some of us didn’t walk away from God.

We just got comfortable enough
to stop walking with Him.
Let me ask you something—be honest:

When was the last time your heart broke over sin?
Not someone else’s… yours.
When was the last time you felt conviction so deep
Or have you learned to silence that voice…
with distractions, success, or “I’m doing okay”?
Amos didn’t show up to entertain.
To expose the lie that comfort equals blessing.

Because sometimes what feels like peace…
is actually distance from God.

God is not against you having comfort—
He’s against comfort having you.

Because when comfort owns you,
you stop noticing what breaks God’s heart.

And when you feel less—
you surrender less.

If your life requires no dependence on God…
you may already be drifting from Him.

Because many of us have built lives
that function perfectly…

Provision without prayer.
Success without surrender.
Worship without obedience.
But heaven might be calling it something else.
This is the kind of message people avoid.
And here’s the piercing line you can’t ignore:

A comfortable Christian with no conviction
is closer to spiritual death than they realize.
Because this isn’t where the story ends.
This is where grace walks in.
God didn’t send Amos to destroy them.
He sent Amos to wake them.
And the same is true for you.

That nudge you feel right now?
That discomfort in your chest?
That’s not guilt trying to crush you.
That’s God trying to call you back.
And this is where Jesus steps in.
Because here’s the Gospel—clear and unfiltered:
The Bible says, “All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23). Not just through rebellion…
But God didn’t leave us there.
Jesus Christ came—not to condemn the comfortable—

He lived the life we failed to live.
Felt what we stopped feeling.
Obeyed where we delayed.
And then He went to the cross—
but our apathy, our numbness, our pride—
and paid for it in full.
“So that whoever believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life” (John 3:16).

Not by works.
Not by effort.
But by grace.
Even if your heart feels cold right now—
He can make it alive again.
Because in Christ, numb hearts beat again.

You are not called to live comfortably numb—
you are called to live fully alive in Christ.

You are not a spectator of faith—
you are a vessel of God’s presence.
Don’t stay in ease while your soul is drifting.

And if you’re hungry to go deeper—
to rebuild a faith that actually feels alive—
to walk with you in real discipleship, not surface religion.
(You’ll find it where hearts are choosing growth over comfort.)
And if this stirred something in you…

It’s for the part of you
you’ve been trying to ignore.
